cover.visual: Stylized California map with a pulsing red alert over a ballot-box icon and a small DOJ seal stamp in the corner.

music.cue: Low-volume tense chiptune enters under the hook, builds slightly through what's-new and known, ducks under every quoted line in the country and world segments, lifts briefly at the unknowns, then fades out under the anchor's final line.

notes: Revision 1 of 2 (per revision_request 4090efb2, Critical 1): S1 narration and on_screen_text restored the 'knowingly' qualifier from F13's quote, so the hook reads as a conditional warning, not an unconditional threat.

Major 2: S6 no longer presents the Newsom line as an English quotation, since the dossier's verbatim quote (W1) is in Spanish and the English text is only a translation note; now paraphrased without quotation marks.

Major 3: metadata title/summary (all platforms) dropped the evaluative word 'Crackdown' and narrowed 'statewide'/'Across California' to 'at least 18 California counties', matching F12's disputed county count.
Minor 4: S2 source_plate now names the outlets behind the scene's facts (Yahoo News AP/CBS, NBC News) instead of 'LA County Registrar', which is not a publisher.
Minor 5: S3 source_plate now cites the Oct. 13-15 primary documents (DOJ complaint, Weber's letter) the scene is actually built on, instead of a single Oct. 24 wire source.
Minor 6: S3 narration 'Weber called the list useless' softened to 'Weber said the list is of no investigative use', matching F6's wording.
Minor 7: S4 narration gives Essayli's documented title at first mention, 'First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli', instead of the vaguer 'a federal prosecutor'.
Minor 8: S5 narration now names Dean Logan as LA County Registrar before his quote, instead of leaving him unnamed while shown on screen.
Minor 9: S6 on_screen_text dropped the quotation marks around 'federal overreach', since that is the dossier's own W1 cluster label, not a press quotation.

Trimmed a few words in S2/S6/S7 and lengthened S1/S3/S4/S5 slightly (duration_s 88->90) to keep every scene at or above 0.37s/word after the above wording fixes, while staying under the 90s channel ceiling and the word budget.

scenes.visual: Anchor at the studio desk; behind her a stylized California map pulses with a blinking red alert icon over a ballot-box icon.
scenes.narration: Federal prosecutors warn California officials: knowingly count noncitizens' ballots, face legal jeopardy.
scenes.on_screen_text: DOJ: knowingly count ballots, face charges

scenes.visual: Camera pans across a pixel-art map of California as small envelope icons fly out from a federal building and land on scattered county pins; a 48-hour clock icon counts down in the corner.
scenes.narration: On Friday, DOJ sent letters to counties across California, ordering ballots from alleged noncitizens set aside within 48 hours. The count is disputed, from 18 to 57 counties. DOJ warned officials who knowingly process them risk prosecution.
scenes.source_plate: Source: Yahoo News (CBS/AP), NBC News · Oct 24

scenes.visual: A sealed thumb drive with a padlock icon sits untouched on a county office desk; nearby, Secretary Weber signs a letter at her own desk as a calendar flips its pages from Oct 13 to Oct 27 and a gavel icon appears.
scenes.narration: On October 13th, DOJ gave LA County a list of 20,000 names it calls likely noncitizens. The county refused to open the password-protected drive. Two days later, DOJ sued to block them. Weber said the list is of no investigative use. A hearing is set for Tuesday, October 27th.
scenes.source_plate: Source: DOJ complaint, Weber letter to DOJ · Oct 13-15

scenes.visual: Bill Essayli stands at a podium with press microphones outside a federal building; a pixel speech bubble with his quote fades in above him.
scenes.narration: The Trump administration says data matching found more than 20,000 likely noncitizens on California's rolls. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said: 'We believe it's at a minimum of 20,000. That's the floor.'

scenes.visual: Split screen: Dean Logan stands behind a county registrar's counter with stacked ballot boxes; Rep. DeSaulnier stands at a podium with the U.S. Capitol dome silhouette; speech bubbles appear in sequence.
scenes.narration: California election officials disagree. LA County Registrar Dean Logan called the new letters a 'posture of intimidation.' Rep. Mark DeSaulnier called it 'the escalating weaponization of the Justice Department.'

scenes.visual: A pixel globe rotates slowly; small newspaper icons pin themselves onto the UK, Spain and Canada. Governor Newsom appears briefly at a podium with a California flag as a dotted line animates toward a Canada icon.
scenes.narration: Coverage abroad differs. The Guardian reports LA officials found many flagged voters born in the U.S. Governor Newsom told El País it is a desperate attempt to suppress Californians' votes. CBC News ties the same crackdown to a dispute with Canada.

scenes.visual: A pixel-art question mark hovers over the California map; two mismatched number tags flicker side by side, then a calendar page circled on Oct 27 spins slowly.
scenes.narration: Questions remain. The exact county count is unclear. LA County's sampling gives conflicting numbers on voters' birthplace. And no one knows how Tuesday's hearing will end.

scenes.visual: Anchor at the studio desk; behind her the screen switches to a plain 'Sources' label as the 8bitnews logo fades in beside it.
scenes.narration: Sources are in the description. Follow for what happens next.

tiktok.title: DOJ Widens Noncitizen-Ballot Demand to California Counties
tiktok.summary: DOJ widened its noncitizen-ballot demand to at least 18 California counties, warning officials they risk prosecution if they knowingly count flagged ballots. This follows DOJ's lawsuit over a disputed list of roughly 20,000 names, with a hearing set for Tuesday.

youtube.title: DOJ Widens Noncitizen-Ballot Demand to California Counties
youtube.summary: DOJ widened its noncitizen-ballot demand from one county to letters sent to at least 18 California counties, warning officials they risk prosecution if they knowingly count flagged ballots. The move follows DOJ's lawsuit against California over a disputed list of roughly 20,000 names, with a court hearing set for Tuesday, October 27th.
